COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
6D CLCON No. 597 of 2025
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Imraj Singh Rautela, Advocate, 
holding brief of Mr. Prateek Tripathi, Advocate 
for the petitioners.
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Brief Holder for the 
State.
The petitioners were reverted from the 
post of Sahayak Nideshak to Sahayak Lekha 
Parikshak Adhikari by an order dated 
19.03.2025 passed by the competent authority. 
That order was challenged by the petitioners in 
WPSB No. 85 of 2025, Birendra Singh Nabiyal 
and others Vs. State of Uttarakhand and others 
(“the petition”), which was allowed on 
30.07.2025 and the Court had set aside the 
order dated 19.03.2025 and directed the 
respondents to permit the petitioners to 
discharge duties on the post of Sahayak 
Nideshak/Lekha Prikshak Adhikari (Grade Pay 
Rs.5400/-, Level-10).
The petitioners have brought to the notice 
of the Court that order dated 30.07.2025, 
passed by the Court in the petition has been 
willfully disobeyed by the respondents and the 
petitioners have not been permitted to discharge 
their duties, as directed by this Court in its 
order dated 30.07.2025.
It is, prima facie, case of contempt.
Issue notice to the respondent no.1 to join 
the proceedings through video conferencing and 
to tell the Court as to why, he should not be 
proceeded for committing contempt of this 
Court and why charges may not be framed 
against him.
List on 19.12.2025.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 28.11.2025
Jitendra

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Fourth Bail Application No. 18 of 2025
Kailash Singh Rawat ….....Applicant
 
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ….….Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Mani Kumar, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. V.S. Rawat, A.G.A. for the State. 
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant is in judicial custody in FIR No.238 of 
2023, under Section 307 IPC, Police Station Nehru Colony, 
District- Dehradun. He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and 
perused.
3. This is the fourth bail application. The first bail 
application, being BA1 No.1222 of 2024, was rejected on 
06.08.2024. The second bail application, being BA2 No.339 
of 2024, was rejected on 26.12.2024. The third bail 
application, being BA3 No.42 of 2025, as also rejected on 
18.09.2025. 
4. Having considered, this Court does not see any 
new ground, which may entitle the applicant to bail. 
Accordingly, the bail application deserves to be rejected. 2
5. The bail application is rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J)
 18.12.2025
Ravi Bisht

Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Prateek Tripathi, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. J.S. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel with 
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
3. Though a response affidavit has been filed by 
respondent-contemnor no.1-Secretary of the 
Department along with Misc. Application (IA No. 
2/2026), whereby it has been stated that promotion 
has been granted to the petitioners.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that 
once the reversion order has been set-aside by the 
Writ Court, petitioners cannot be granted promotion 
from 20.03.2026, rather, they would be deemed to 
have been promoted when they were promoted 
earlier, before the reversion order was passed.
5. The contention of the petitioners is quite legal, 
and the action on the part of the respondents￾contemnors is contrary to the law and against the 
spirit of the order passed by the Writ Court. Despite 
being at the office of the Secretary level, such an  absurd order has been passed by him. It is expected 
that the respondents-contemnors or the responsible 
officer in the department shall pass a fresh order of 
promotion of the petitioners within three weeks.
6. List on 07.10.2026.
7. In the meantime, petitioners shall file an 
application for impleading the new incumbent￾Secretary as respondent-contemnor.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
